structures.name: Abductor digiti minimi (foot)
structures.summary: Abducts the fifth toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint. Supplied by the lateral plantar nerve.

structures.name: Abductor digiti minimi (hand)
structures.summary: Abducts the little finger at the metacarpophalangeal joint. Supplied by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.

structures.name: Abductor hallucis
structures.summary: Abducts the great toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint. Supplied by the medial plantar nerve.

structures.name: Abductor pollicis brevis
structures.summary: Abducts the thumb at the carpometacarpal and metacarpophalangeal joints (moves it anteriorly, perpendicular to the palm). Supplied by the recurrent (thenar) branch of the median nerve.

structures.name: Abductor pollicis longus
structures.summary: Abducts and extends the thumb at the carpometacarpal joint. Supplied by the posterior interosseous nerve.

structures.name: Adductor brevis
structures.summary: Adducts the hip. Supplied by the obturator nerve, anterior branch.

structures.name: Adductor longus
structures.summary: Adducts the hip. Supplied by the anterior branch of the obturator nerve.

structures.name: Adductor magnus
structures.summary: Adducts the hip. Supplied by the obturator nerve, posterior branch for the adductor part, and the tibial division of the sciatic nerve for the hamstring part.

structures.name: Adductor pollicis
structures.summary: Adducts the thumb at the carpometacarpal joint. Supplied by the ulnar nerve, deep branch.

structures.name: Adrenal gland
structures.summary: Sits on top of the kidney and releases adrenaline and cortisol.

structures.name: Anterior auricular muscle
structures.summary: Draws the auricle forward and slightly upward. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), temporal branch.

structures.name: Anterior scalene
actions: Bends the neck to the side
structures.summary: Elevates the first rib (accessory inspiration). Supplied by anterior rami of cervical spinal nerves.

structures.name: Atlas (C1 vertebra)
structures.summary: The first neck vertebra (C1), a ring of bone that carries the skull. Muscles attached include the splenius cervicis and levator scapulae.

structures.name: Axis (C2 vertebra)
structures.summary: The second neck vertebra (C2); the head turns around its upward peg, the dens. Muscles attached include the splenius cervicis, levator scapulae and middle scalene.

structures.name: Biceps brachii
structures.summary: Supinates the forearm (most powerfully with the elbow flexed) and flexes the elbow. Supplied by the musculocutaneous nerve.

structures.name: Biceps femoris
structures.summary: Flexes the knee. Its long head extends the hip. Supplied by the tibial division of the sciatic nerve for the long head, and the common fibular division of the sciatic nerve for the short head.

structures.name: Brachialis
structures.summary: The main flexor of the elbow, whatever the position of the forearm. Supplied by the musculocutaneous nerve.

structures.name: Brachioradialis
structures.summary: Flexes the elbow, most effectively with the forearm in the mid-prone (neutral) position. Supplied by the radial nerve.

structures.name: Brainstem
structures.summary: Links the brain to the spinal cord and controls breathing, heart rate and other vital functions.

structures.name: Buccinator
actions: Presses the cheek against the teeth
structures.summary: Presses the cheek against the molar teeth. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), buccal branch.

structures.name: C3 vertebra
structures.summary: The third of the seven neck (cervical) vertebrae. Muscles attached include the levator scapulae, middle scalene and anterior scalene.

structures.name: C4 vertebra
structures.summary: The fourth of the seven neck (cervical) vertebrae. Muscles attached include the levator scapulae, middle scalene and posterior scalene.

structures.name: C5 vertebra
structures.summary: The fifth of the seven neck (cervical) vertebrae. Muscles attached include the middle scalene, posterior scalene and anterior scalene.

structures.name: C6 vertebra
structures.summary: The sixth of the seven neck (cervical) vertebrae. Muscles attached include the middle scalene, posterior scalene and anterior scalene.

structures.name: C7 vertebra
structures.summary: The seventh of the seven neck (cervical) vertebrae, whose long spinous process is the bump at the base of the neck. Muscles attached include the trapezius, rhomboid minor and middle scalene.

structures.name: Calcaneus (heel bone)
structures.summary: The heel bone, the largest bone of the foot. Muscles attached include the gastrocnemius, flexor digitorum brevis and abductor hallucis.

structures.name: Carpal bones
structures.summary: The eight small bones of the wrist, in two rows between the forearm and the palm. Muscles attached include the flexor carpi ulnaris, abductor digiti minimi (hand) and adductor pollicis.

structures.name: Cerebellum
structures.summary: Coordinates movement, balance and posture. It sits at the back of the brain, under the cerebrum.

structures.name: Cerebrum
structures.summary: The largest part of the brain: two hemispheres in charge of thought, movement, sensation and language.

structures.name: Clavicle
structures.summary: The collarbone, a horizontal strut between the sternum and the shoulder blade. Muscles attached include the trapezius, pectoralis major and deltoid.

structures.name: Large intestine (colon)
structures.summary: The large intestine: it absorbs water and salts from what is left of the food and forms stool.

structures.name: Coracobrachialis
structures.summary: Flexes and adducts the arm at the shoulder. Supplied by the musculocutaneous nerve.

structures.name: Corrugator supercilii
structures.summary: Draws the eyebrows medially and downward, producing vertical glabellar wrinkles (frowning). Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), temporal branch.

structures.name: Cuboid
structures.summary: A cube-shaped bone on the outer side of the foot, just in front of the calcaneus.

structures.name: Deltoid
structures.summary: Its acromial (middle) part abducts the arm at the shoulder. Supplied by the axillary nerve.

structures.name: Depressor anguli oris
actions: Pulls the corners of the mouth down
structures.summary: Draws the angle of the mouth downward and laterally. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), marginal mandibular and buccal branches.

structures.name: Depressor labii inferioris
structures.summary: Depresses the lower lip and draws it laterally. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), marginal mandibular branch.

structures.name: Depressor septi nasi
actions: Pulls the tip of the nose down
structures.summary: Draws the nasal septum (columella) and nasal tip downwards. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), buccal branch.

structures.name: Depressor supercilii
structures.summary: Depresses the medial end of the eyebrow. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), temporal and zygomatic branches.

structures.name: Diaphragm
structures.summary: Descends and flattens to enlarge the thoracic cavity vertically (principal muscle of inspiration). Supplied by the phrenic nerve.

structures.name: Digastric
structures.summary: Depresses the mandible (opens the mouth) when the hyoid is fixed. Supplied by the nerve to mylohyoid from the mandibular nerve (CN V3) for the anterior belly, and the facial nerve (CN VII), digastric branch for the posterior belly.

structures.name: Distal phalanx of fifth toe
structures.summary: The tip bone of the fifth toe. Muscles attached include the flexor digitorum longus.

structures.name: Distal phalanx of fourth toe
structures.summary: The tip bone of the fourth toe. Muscles attached include the flexor digitorum longus.

structures.name: Distal phalanx of great toe
structures.summary: The tip bone of the great toe. Muscles attached include the flexor hallucis longus.

structures.name: Distal phalanx of index finger
structures.summary: The tip bone of the index finger. Muscles attached include the extensor indicis.

structures.name: Distal phalanx of little finger
structures.summary: The tip bone of the little finger.

structures.name: Distal phalanx of middle finger
structures.summary: The tip bone of the middle finger.

structures.name: Distal phalanx of ring finger
structures.summary: The tip bone of the ring finger.

structures.name: Distal phalanx of second toe
structures.summary: The tip bone of the second toe. Muscles attached include the flexor digitorum longus.

structures.name: Distal phalanx of third toe
structures.summary: The tip bone of the third toe. Muscles attached include the flexor digitorum longus.

structures.name: Distal phalanx of thumb
structures.summary: The tip bone of the thumb. Muscles attached include the flexor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis longus.

structures.name: Dorsal interossei (hand)
structures.summary: Abduct the index, middle and ring fingers at the metacarpophalangeal joints, away from the axis of the middle finger. Supplied by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.

structures.name: Eighth rib
structures.summary: The eighth of the twelve pairs of ribs, a false rib, whose cartilage joins the rib above. Muscles attached include the serratus anterior and external oblique.

structures.name: Eleventh rib
structures.summary: The eleventh of the twelve pairs of ribs, a floating rib, with a free front end. Muscles attached include the external oblique and internal oblique.

structures.name: Extensor carpi radialis brevis
structures.summary: Extends and abducts (radially deviates) the wrist. Supplied by the deep branch of the radial nerve.

structures.name: Extensor carpi radialis longus
structures.summary: Extends and abducts (radially deviates) the wrist. Supplied by the radial nerve.

structures.name: Extensor carpi ulnaris
structures.summary: Extends and adducts (ulnar deviates) the wrist. Supplied by the posterior interosseous nerve.

structures.name: Extensor digitorum
structures.summary: Extends the medial four fingers at the metacarpophalangeal joints. Supplied by the posterior interosseous nerve.

structures.name: Extensor digitorum brevis
structures.summary: Extends the second to fourth toes at the metatarsophalangeal and interphalangeal joints. Supplied by the deep fibular nerve, lateral branch.

structures.name: Extensor digitorum longus
structures.summary: Extends the lateral four toes at the metatarsophalangeal and interphalangeal joints and dorsiflexes the ankle. Supplied by the deep fibular nerve.

structures.name: Extensor hallucis brevis
structures.summary: Extends the great toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint. Supplied by the deep fibular nerve, lateral terminal branch.

structures.name: Extensor hallucis longus
structures.summary: Extends the great toe at the metatarsophalangeal and interphalangeal joints and dorsiflexes the ankle. Supplied by the deep fibular nerve.

structures.name: Extensor indicis
structures.summary: Extends the index finger independently of the other fingers. Supplied by the posterior interosseous nerve.

structures.name: Extensor pollicis brevis
structures.summary: Extends the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal joint. Supplied by the posterior interosseous nerve.

structures.name: Extensor pollicis longus
structures.summary: Extends the thumb at the interphalangeal joint and extends the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal and carpometacarpal joints. Supplied by the posterior interosseous nerve.

structures.name: External intercostals
structures.summary: Elevate the ribs during inspiration. Supplied by the intercostal nerves.

structures.name: External oblique
actions: Bends the trunk to the side
structures.summary: Flexes the trunk (both sides together) and rotates the trunk to the opposite side (one side acting). Supplied by the thoraco-abdominal nerves and subcostal nerve.

structures.name: Eyeball
structures.summary: The organ of sight: its cornea and lens focus light onto the retina at the back.

structures.name: Femur
structures.summary: The thigh bone, the longest and strongest bone of the body. Muscles attached include the vastus lateralis, adductor magnus and gluteus maximus.

structures.name: Fibula
structures.summary: The slender bone on the outer side of the leg; its lower end forms the outer ankle bump. Muscles attached include the soleus, extensor digitorum longus and fibularis longus.

structures.name: Fibularis brevis
structures.summary: Everts the foot at the subtalar and transverse tarsal joints. Supplied by the superficial fibular nerve.

structures.name: Fibularis longus
structures.summary: Everts the foot and plantar flexes the ankle. Supplied by the superficial fibular nerve.

structures.name: Fifth metacarpal
structures.summary: One of the five long bones of the palm, the one that leads to the little finger. Muscles attached include the flexor carpi ulnaris, extensor carpi ulnaris and dorsal interossei (hand).

structures.name: Fifth metatarsal
structures.summary: One of the five long bones of the sole of the foot, the one that leads to the fifth toe. Muscles attached include the fibularis brevis.

structures.name: Fifth rib
structures.summary: The fifth of the twelve pairs of ribs, a true rib, joined to the sternum by its own cartilage. Muscles attached include the serratus anterior, pectoralis minor and external oblique.

structures.name: First metacarpal
structures.summary: One of the five long bones of the palm, the one that leads to the thumb. Muscles attached include the abductor pollicis longus and dorsal interossei (hand).

structures.name: First metatarsal
structures.summary: One of the five long bones of the sole of the foot, the one that leads to the great toe. Muscles attached include the tibialis anterior and fibularis longus.

structures.name: First rib
structures.summary: The first of the twelve pairs of ribs, a true rib, joined to the sternum by its own cartilage. Muscles attached include the serratus anterior, middle scalene and anterior scalene.

structures.name: Flexor carpi radialis
structures.summary: Flexes and abducts (radially deviates) the wrist. Supplied by the median nerve.

structures.name: Flexor carpi ulnaris
structures.summary: Flexes and adducts (ulnar deviates) the wrist. Supplied by the ulnar nerve.

structures.name: Flexor digiti minimi brevis (hand)
structures.latin: Musculus flexor digiti minimi brevis manus
structures.summary: Flexes the little finger at the metacarpophalangeal joint. Supplied by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.

structures.name: Flexor digitorum brevis
structures.summary: Flexes the lateral four toes at the proximal interphalangeal joints. Supplied by the medial plantar nerve.

structures.name: Flexor digitorum longus
structures.summary: Flexes the second to fifth toes, mainly at the distal interphalangeal joints. Supplied by the tibial nerve.

structures.name: Flexor digitorum profundus
structures.summary: Flexes the distal interphalangeal joints of fingers 2–5 (the only muscle able to do so). Supplied by the ulnar nerve for the medial part (fingers 4–5), and the anterior interosseous nerve for the lateral part (fingers 2–3).

structures.name: Flexor digitorum superficialis
structures.summary: Flexes the proximal interphalangeal joints of fingers 2–5. Supplied by the median nerve.

structures.name: Flexor hallucis longus
structures.summary: Flexes the great toe at the interphalangeal and metatarsophalangeal joints. Supplied by the tibial nerve.

structures.name: Flexor pollicis brevis
structures.summary: Flexes the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal joint. Supplied by the recurrent branch of the median nerve for the superficial head, and the deep branch of the ulnar nerve for the deep head.

structures.name: Flexor pollicis longus
structures.summary: Flexes the interphalangeal joint of the thumb. Supplied by the anterior interosseous nerve.

structures.name: Fourth metacarpal
structures.summary: One of the five long bones of the palm, the one that leads to the ring finger. Muscles attached include the dorsal interossei (hand).

structures.name: Fourth metatarsal
structures.summary: One of the five long bones of the sole of the foot, the one that leads to the fourth toe.

structures.name: Fourth rib
structures.summary: The fourth of the twelve pairs of ribs, a true rib, joined to the sternum by its own cartilage. Muscles attached include the serratus anterior and pectoralis minor.

structures.name: Frontalis
structures.summary: Raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the forehead horizontally. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), temporal branch.

structures.name: Gallbladder
structures.summary: Stores and concentrates bile made by the liver, and releases it into the duodenum after a meal.

structures.name: Gastrocnemius
structures.summary: Plantar flexes the ankle, most strongly with the knee extended. Supplied by the tibial nerve.

structures.name: Gluteus maximus
structures.summary: Extends the hip (especially from flexion: rising from sitting, climbing stairs) and laterally rotates the hip. Supplied by the inferior gluteal nerve.

structures.name: Gluteus medius
structures.summary: Abducts the hip. Supplied by the superior gluteal nerve.

structures.name: Gluteus minimus
structures.summary: Abducts and medially rotates the hip. Supplied by the superior gluteal nerve.

structures.name: Gracilis
structures.summary: Adducts the hip. Supplied by the obturator nerve, anterior branch.

structures.name: Heart
structures.summary: Pumps blood through the lungs and around the body. It sits behind the sternum, between the two lungs.

structures.name: Hip bone
structures.summary: The large bone of each side of the pelvis, formed by the fused ilium, ischium and pubis. Muscles attached include the gluteus maximus, gluteus medius and iliacus.

structures.name: Humerus
structures.summary: The long bone of the arm, from the shoulder to the elbow. Muscles attached include the triceps brachii, brachialis and brachioradialis.

structures.name: Hyoglossus
structures.summary: Depresses and retracts the tongue. Supplied by the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).

structures.name: Iliacus
structures.summary: Flexes the hip. Supplied by the femoral nerve.

structures.name: Iliocostalis
actions: Bends the trunk to the side
structures.summary: Extends the vertebral column when both sides work together. Supplied by lateral branches of the dorsal (posterior) rami of the cervical, thoracic and lumbar spinal nerves.

structures.name: Inferior gemellus
structures.summary: Laterally rotates the extended hip. Supplied by the nerve to quadratus femoris.

structures.name: Infraspinatus
structures.summary: Laterally rotates the shoulder. Supplied by the suprascapular nerve.

structures.name: Intermediate cuneiform
structures.summary: One of the three wedge-shaped cuneiform bones of the midfoot, the smallest, in the middle, in front of the navicular. Muscles attached include the tibialis posterior.

structures.name: Internal intercostals
structures.summary: Its interosseous (lateral) parts depress the ribs during forced expiration. Supplied by the intercostal nerves.

structures.name: Internal oblique
actions: Bends the trunk to the side
structures.summary: Compresses the abdominal viscera and rotates the trunk to the same side (with the contralateral external oblique). Supplied by the thoraco-abdominal nerves, subcostal nerve, iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal nerves.

structures.name: Kidney
structures.summary: Filters the blood to make urine, keeping water, salts and blood pressure in balance.

structures.name: L1 vertebra
structures.summary: The first of the five lumbar vertebrae, the largest of the spine. Muscles attached include the latissimus dorsi, quadratus lumborum and diaphragm.

structures.name: L2 vertebra
structures.summary: The second of the five lumbar vertebrae, the largest of the spine. Muscles attached include the latissimus dorsi, quadratus lumborum and diaphragm.

structures.name: L3 vertebra
structures.summary: The third of the five lumbar vertebrae, the largest of the spine. Muscles attached include the latissimus dorsi, quadratus lumborum and diaphragm.

structures.name: L4 vertebra
structures.summary: The fourth of the five lumbar vertebrae, the largest of the spine. Muscles attached include the latissimus dorsi, quadratus lumborum and psoas major.

structures.name: L5 vertebra
structures.summary: The lowest of the five lumbar vertebrae, the largest of the spine, resting on the sacrum. Muscles attached include the latissimus dorsi and psoas major.

structures.name: Lateral cuneiform
structures.summary: One of the three wedge-shaped cuneiform bones of the midfoot, the one on the outer side, in front of the navicular. Muscles attached include the tibialis posterior.

structures.name: Latissimus dorsi
structures.summary: Extends, adducts and medially rotates the shoulder. Supplied by the thoracodorsal nerve.

structures.name: Levator anguli oris
actions: Pulls the corners of the mouth up
structures.summary: Elevates the angle of the mouth. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), zygomatic and buccal branches.

structures.name: Levator labii superioris
structures.summary: Elevates the upper lip. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), zygomatic and buccal branches.

structures.name: Levator labii superioris alaeque nasi
structures.latin: Musculus levator labii superioris alaeque nasi
structures.summary: Elevates the upper lip and dilates the nostril by raising the ala of the nose. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), zygomatic and buccal branches.

structures.name: Levator scapulae
actions: Bends the neck to the side
structures.summary: Elevates the scapula and rotates the scapula downward (tilts the glenoid cavity inferiorly). Supplied by the dorsal scapular nerve and anterior rami of C3–C4.

structures.name: Liver
structures.summary: Makes bile, stores sugar as glycogen and processes the blood coming from the gut. The largest internal organ.

structures.name: Longissimus
actions: Bends the trunk to the side
Bends the neck to the side
structures.summary: Extends the vertebral column, and the head (capitis part) when both sides work together. Supplied by lateral branches of the posterior rami of the cervical, thoracic and lumbar spinal nerves.

structures.name: Lumbricals (hand)
structures.summary: Flex the metacarpophalangeal joints and extend the interphalangeal joints of fingers 2–5. Supplied by the median nerve for the first and second, and the deep branch of the ulnar nerve for the third and fourth.

structures.name: Lung
structures.summary: Takes oxygen into the blood and removes carbon dioxide. The right lung has three lobes, the left lung two.

structures.name: Mandible
structures.summary: The lower jaw, the only skull bone that moves; it carries the lower teeth. Muscles attached include the temporalis, orbicularis oris and buccinator.

structures.name: Masseter
structures.summary: Elevates the mandible (closes the jaw). Supplied by the masseteric nerve from the mandibular nerve (CN V3).

structures.name: Medial cuneiform
structures.summary: One of the three wedge-shaped cuneiform bones of the midfoot, the largest, on the inner side, in front of the navicular. Muscles attached include the tibialis anterior, fibularis longus and tibialis posterior.

structures.name: Mentalis
structures.summary: Elevates and wrinkles the skin of the chin and elevates and protrudes the lower lip. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), marginal mandibular branch.

structures.name: Middle phalanx of fifth toe
structures.summary: The middle bone of the fifth toe. Muscles attached include the flexor digitorum brevis.

structures.name: Middle phalanx of fourth toe
structures.summary: The middle bone of the fourth toe.

structures.name: Middle phalanx of index finger
structures.summary: The middle bone of the index finger.

structures.name: Middle phalanx of little finger
structures.summary: The middle bone of the little finger.

structures.name: Middle phalanx of middle finger
structures.summary: The middle bone of the middle finger.

structures.name: Middle phalanx of ring finger
structures.summary: The middle bone of the ring finger.

structures.name: Middle phalanx of second toe
structures.summary: The middle bone of the second toe. Muscles attached include the flexor digitorum brevis.

structures.name: Middle phalanx of third toe
structures.summary: The middle bone of the third toe. Muscles attached include the flexor digitorum brevis.

structures.name: Middle scalene
actions: Bends the neck to the side
structures.summary: Elevates the first rib in forced inspiration and laterally flexes the neck to the same side. Supplied by anterior rami of cervical spinal nerves.

structures.name: Mylohyoid
structures.summary: Elevates the floor of the mouth and the hyoid bone during swallowing and speech. Supplied by the nerve to mylohyoid.

structures.name: Nasalis
structures.summary: Its transverse part compresses the nasal aperture. Its alar part flares (dilates) the nostril. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), buccal branch.

structures.name: Navicular bone (foot)
structures.summary: A boat-shaped bone on the inner side of the foot, just in front of the talus. Muscles attached include the tibialis posterior.

structures.name: Ninth rib
structures.summary: The ninth of the twelve pairs of ribs, a false rib, whose cartilage joins the rib above. Muscles attached include the external oblique.

structures.name: Obturator externus
structures.summary: Laterally rotates the hip. Supplied by the obturator nerve, posterior branch.

structures.name: Obturator internus
structures.summary: Laterally rotates the extended hip. Supplied by the nerve to obturator internus.

structures.name: Omohyoid
structures.summary: Depresses the hyoid bone. Supplied by the ansa cervicalis.

structures.name: Opponens digiti minimi
structures.summary: Opposes the little finger. Supplied by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.

structures.name: Opponens pollicis
structures.summary: Opposes the thumb by flexing and medially rotating the first metacarpal at the carpometacarpal joint. Supplied by the recurrent (thenar) branch of the median nerve.

structures.name: Orbicularis oculi
structures.summary: Closes the eyelids. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), temporal and zygomatic branches.

structures.name: Orbicularis oris
structures.summary: Closes and protrudes (purses) the lips. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), buccal and marginal mandibular branches.

structures.name: Palmar interossei
structures.summary: Adduct the index, ring and little fingers towards the axis of the middle finger at the metacarpophalangeal joints. Supplied by the ulnar nerve, deep branch.

structures.name: Palmaris longus
structures.summary: Flexes the wrist. Supplied by the median nerve.

structures.name: Pancreas
structures.summary: Releases digestive enzymes into the duodenum and the hormones insulin and glucagon into the blood.

structures.name: Patella (kneecap)
structures.summary: The kneecap, a bone set in the quadriceps tendon in front of the knee. Muscles attached include the vastus lateralis, vastus medialis and vastus intermedius.

structures.name: Pectineus
structures.summary: Adducts and flexes the hip. Supplied by the femoral nerve.

structures.name: Pectoralis major
structures.summary: Adducts and medially rotates the arm at the shoulder. Supplied by the lateral pectoral nerve and medial pectoral nerve.

structures.name: Pectoralis minor
structures.summary: Draws the scapula forward and downward (protraction and depression). Supplied by the medial pectoral nerve.

structures.name: Piriformis
structures.summary: Laterally rotates the extended hip. Supplied by the nerve to piriformis.

structures.name: Platysma
actions: Tenses the skin of the neck
Pulls the corners of the mouth down
structures.summary: Tenses the skin of the neck, raising vertical ridges. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), cervical branch.

structures.name: Posterior auricular muscle
structures.summary: Draws the auricle backward. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), posterior auricular branch.

structures.name: Posterior scalene
actions: Bends the neck to the side
structures.summary: Elevates the second rib (accessory inspiration) and laterally flexes the cervical spine (one side acting). Supplied by anterior rami of cervical spinal nerves.

structures.name: Procerus
structures.summary: Draws the medial ends of the eyebrows downward. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), temporal and zygomatic branches.

structures.name: Pronator quadratus
structures.summary: Pronates the forearm. Supplied by the anterior interosseous nerve.

structures.name: Pronator teres
structures.summary: Pronates the forearm. Supplied by the median nerve.

structures.name: Prostate
structures.summary: A gland under the bladder, around the urethra, that adds fluid to semen.

structures.name: Proximal phalanx of fifth toe
structures.summary: The bone at the base of the fifth toe. Muscles attached include the abductor digiti minimi (foot).

structures.name: Proximal phalanx of fourth toe
structures.summary: The bone at the base of the fourth toe. Muscles attached include the extensor digitorum brevis.

structures.name: Proximal phalanx of great toe
structures.summary: The bone at the base of the great toe. Muscles attached include the extensor hallucis longus, abductor hallucis and extensor hallucis brevis.

structures.name: Proximal phalanx of index finger
structures.summary: The bone at the base of the index finger.

structures.name: Proximal phalanx of little finger
structures.summary: The bone at the base of the little finger. Muscles attached include the abductor digiti minimi (hand).

structures.name: Proximal phalanx of middle finger
structures.summary: The bone at the base of the middle finger.

structures.name: Proximal phalanx of ring finger
structures.summary: The bone at the base of the ring finger.

structures.name: Proximal phalanx of second toe
structures.summary: The bone at the base of the second toe. Muscles attached include the extensor digitorum brevis.

structures.name: Proximal phalanx of third toe
structures.summary: The bone at the base of the third toe. Muscles attached include the extensor digitorum brevis.

structures.name: Proximal phalanx of thumb
structures.summary: The bone at the base of the thumb. Muscles attached include the extensor pollicis brevis and adductor pollicis.

structures.name: Psoas major
structures.summary: Flexes the hip (with iliacus as iliopsoas). Supplied by anterior rami of the lumbar nerves.

structures.name: Psoas minor
structures.summary: Weakly flexes the lumbar vertebral column on the pelvis. Supplied by the anterior ramus of L1.

structures.name: Quadratus lumborum
actions: Bends the trunk to the side
structures.summary: Laterally flexes the lumbar spine (one side acting). Supplied by anterior rami of T12–L4 (subcostal and lumbar nerves).

structures.name: Radius
structures.summary: The forearm bone on the thumb side; it turns around the ulna when the palm turns over. Muscles attached include the flexor digitorum superficialis, brachioradialis and abductor pollicis longus.

structures.name: Rectus abdominis
structures.summary: Flexes the trunk (lumbar spine). Supplied by the thoraco-abdominal nerves and subcostal nerve.

structures.name: Rectus femoris
structures.summary: Extends the knee and flexes the hip. Supplied by the femoral nerve.

structures.name: Rhomboid major
structures.summary: Retracts (adducts) the scapula and rotates the scapula downward (glenoid cavity turned inferiorly). Supplied by the dorsal scapular nerve.

structures.name: Rhomboid minor
structures.summary: Retracts the scapula and rotates the scapula downward (tilts the glenoid cavity inferiorly). Supplied by the dorsal scapular nerve.

structures.name: Risorius
actions: Pulls the corners of the mouth sideways
structures.summary: Draws the angle of the mouth laterally. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), buccal branch.

structures.name: Sacrum
structures.summary: The triangular bone at the base of the spine, made of five fused vertebrae and wedged between the hip bones. Muscles attached include the gluteus maximus, piriformis and latissimus dorsi.

structures.name: Sartorius
structures.summary: Flexes the hip and flexes the knee. Supplied by the femoral nerve.

structures.name: Scapula
structures.summary: The shoulder blade, a flat triangular bone on the back of the rib cage whose socket holds the head of the humerus. Muscles attached include the trapezius, serratus anterior and deltoid.

structures.name: Second metacarpal
structures.summary: One of the five long bones of the palm, the one that leads to the index finger. Muscles attached include the flexor carpi radialis, extensor carpi radialis longus and dorsal interossei (hand).

structures.name: Second metatarsal
structures.summary: One of the five long bones of the sole of the foot, the one that leads to the second toe.

structures.name: Second rib
structures.summary: The second of the twelve pairs of ribs, a true rib, joined to the sternum by its own cartilage. Muscles attached include the serratus anterior and posterior scalene.

structures.name: Semimembranosus
structures.summary: Extends the hip and flexes the knee. Supplied by the tibial division of the sciatic nerve.

structures.name: Semispinalis capitis
structures.summary: Extends the head at the atlanto-occipital joint and the upper cervical spine (bilateral contraction). Supplied by medial branches of the posterior rami of the cervical spinal nerves.

structures.name: Semispinalis cervicis
structures.summary: Extends the cervical spine (both sides acting). Supplied by medial branches of the posterior (dorsal) rami of the cervical spinal nerves.

structures.name: Semitendinosus
structures.summary: One of the hamstrings: extends the hip and flexes the knee. Supplied by the tibial part of the sciatic nerve.

structures.name: Serratus anterior
structures.summary: Protracts the scapula and rotates the scapula upward (inferior fibres). Supplied by the long thoracic nerve.

structures.name: Seventh rib
structures.summary: The seventh of the twelve pairs of ribs, a true rib, joined to the sternum by its own cartilage. Muscles attached include the serratus anterior and external oblique.

structures.name: Sixth rib
structures.summary: The sixth of the twelve pairs of ribs, a true rib, joined to the sternum by its own cartilage. Muscles attached include the serratus anterior and external oblique.

structures.name: Skull
structures.summary: The bony case of the head that protects the brain and holds the eyes, ears and upper teeth. Muscles attached include the temporalis, buccinator and procerus.

structures.name: Small intestine
structures.summary: Where most food is digested and absorbed. Its folds and villi give it a huge inner surface.

structures.name: Soleus
structures.summary: Plantar flexes the ankle, whatever the position of the knee. Supplied by the tibial nerve.

structures.name: Spinalis
structures.summary: Extends the vertebral column (both sides acting). Supplied by lateral branches of the posterior (dorsal) rami of the spinal nerves.

structures.name: Spleen
structures.summary: Filters the blood, removes worn-out red blood cells and helps fight infection.

structures.name: Splenius capitis
actions: Bends the neck to the side
structures.summary: Extends the head and neck when both sides work together. Supplied by lateral branches of the dorsal (posterior) rami of the middle cervical spinal nerves.

structures.name: Splenius cervicis
actions: Bends the neck to the side
structures.summary: Extends the neck (bilateral contraction) and laterally flexes and rotates the neck to the same side (unilateral contraction). Supplied by lateral branches of the posterior rami of the middle and lower cervical spinal nerves.

structures.name: Sternocleidomastoid
actions: Bends the neck to the side
structures.summary: Tilts the head toward the same shoulder and rotates the face to the opposite side when one side works alone. Supplied by the accessory nerve (CN XI).

structures.name: Sternohyoid
structures.summary: Depresses the hyoid bone (after it has been raised in swallowing). Supplied by the ansa cervicalis.

structures.name: Sternothyroid
structures.summary: Depresses the larynx (thyroid cartilage) after it has been elevated in swallowing or speech. Supplied by the ansa cervicalis.

structures.name: Sternum
structures.summary: The breastbone, in the front of the chest; the upper ribs join it through their cartilages. Muscles attached include the diaphragm, pectoralis major and rectus abdominis.

structures.name: Stomach
structures.summary: Stores food and starts digesting it with acid and enzymes before passing it on to the small intestine.

structures.name: Stylohyoid
structures.summary: Elevates and retracts the hyoid bone. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), stylohyoid branch.

structures.name: Subscapularis
structures.summary: Medially rotates the shoulder (humerus). Supplied by the upper and lower subscapular nerves.

structures.name: Superior auricular muscle
structures.summary: Elevates the auricle. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), temporal branch.

structures.name: Superior gemellus
structures.summary: Laterally rotates the extended hip. Supplied by the nerve to obturator internus.

structures.name: Supraspinatus
structures.summary: Abducts the arm at the shoulder, acting with the deltoid from the start of the movement. Supplied by the suprascapular nerve.

structures.name: T1 vertebra
structures.summary: The first of the twelve thoracic vertebrae, in the upper back; it carries the first pair of ribs. Muscles attached include the trapezius and rhomboid minor.

structures.name: T10 vertebra
structures.summary: The tenth of the twelve thoracic vertebrae, in the lower back; it carries the tenth pair of ribs. Muscles attached include the latissimus dorsi and trapezius.

structures.name: T11 vertebra
structures.summary: The eleventh of the twelve thoracic vertebrae, in the lower back; it carries the eleventh pair of ribs. Muscles attached include the latissimus dorsi and trapezius.

structures.name: T12 vertebra
structures.summary: The twelfth of the twelve thoracic vertebrae, in the lower back; it carries the twelfth pair of ribs. Muscles attached include the latissimus dorsi, trapezius and psoas major.

structures.name: T2 vertebra
structures.summary: The second of the twelve thoracic vertebrae, in the upper back; it carries the second pair of ribs. Muscles attached include the trapezius and rhomboid major.

structures.name: T3 vertebra
structures.summary: The third of the twelve thoracic vertebrae, in the upper back; it carries the third pair of ribs. Muscles attached include the trapezius and rhomboid major.

structures.name: T4 vertebra
structures.summary: The fourth of the twelve thoracic vertebrae, in the upper back; it carries the fourth pair of ribs. Muscles attached include the trapezius and rhomboid major.

structures.name: T5 vertebra
structures.summary: The fifth of the twelve thoracic vertebrae, in the middle back; it carries the fifth pair of ribs. Muscles attached include the trapezius and rhomboid major.

structures.name: T6 vertebra
structures.summary: The sixth of the twelve thoracic vertebrae, in the middle back; it carries the sixth pair of ribs. Muscles attached include the trapezius.

structures.name: T7 vertebra
structures.summary: The seventh of the twelve thoracic vertebrae, in the middle back; it carries the seventh pair of ribs. Muscles attached include the latissimus dorsi and trapezius.

structures.name: T8 vertebra
structures.summary: The eighth of the twelve thoracic vertebrae, in the middle back; it carries the eighth pair of ribs. Muscles attached include the latissimus dorsi and trapezius.

structures.name: T9 vertebra
structures.summary: The ninth of the twelve thoracic vertebrae, in the lower back; it carries the ninth pair of ribs. Muscles attached include the latissimus dorsi and trapezius.

structures.name: Talus (ankle bone)
structures.summary: The ankle bone that links the leg to the foot, between the tibia, the fibula and the calcaneus.

structures.name: Temporalis
structures.summary: Elevates the mandible (closes the jaw). Supplied by the mandibular nerve (CN V3), deep temporal branches.

structures.name: Tensor fasciae latae
structures.summary: Abducts and medially rotates the hip and tenses the fascia lata and iliotibial tract. Supplied by the superior gluteal nerve.

structures.name: Tenth rib
structures.summary: The tenth of the twelve pairs of ribs, a false rib, whose cartilage joins the rib above. Muscles attached include the external oblique and internal oblique.

structures.name: Teres major
structures.summary: Adducts and medially rotates the arm at the shoulder. Supplied by the lower subscapular nerve.

structures.name: Teres minor
structures.summary: Laterally rotates the shoulder. Supplied by the axillary nerve.

structures.name: Testis
structures.summary: Produces sperm and the hormone testosterone.

structures.name: Third metacarpal
structures.summary: One of the five long bones of the palm, the one that leads to the middle finger. Muscles attached include the flexor carpi radialis, extensor carpi radialis brevis and dorsal interossei (hand).

structures.name: Third metatarsal
structures.summary: One of the five long bones of the sole of the foot, the one that leads to the third toe.

structures.name: Third rib
structures.summary: The third of the twelve pairs of ribs, a true rib, joined to the sternum by its own cartilage. Muscles attached include the serratus anterior and pectoralis minor.

structures.name: Thymus
structures.summary: Trains the T cells of the immune system. Large in children, it shrinks after puberty.

structures.name: Thyrohyoid
structures.summary: Depresses the hyoid bone and elevates the larynx when the hyoid is fixed. Supplied by C1 fibres carried by the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII), nerve to thyrohyoid.

structures.name: Tibia
structures.summary: The shin bone, the larger of the two leg bones, which carries the body's weight to the ankle. Muscles attached include the soleus, extensor digitorum longus and tibialis anterior.

structures.name: Tibialis anterior
structures.summary: Dorsiflexes the ankle and inverts the foot. Supplied by the deep fibular nerve.

structures.name: Tibialis posterior
structures.summary: Inverts the foot and plantar flexes the ankle. Supplied by the tibial nerve.

structures.name: Tongue
structures.summary: A muscular organ that moves food for chewing and swallowing, carries the taste buds and shapes speech.

structures.name: Trachea
structures.summary: The windpipe: a tube held open by rings of cartilage that carries air from the larynx to the two main bronchi.

structures.name: Transversus abdominis
structures.summary: Compresses and supports the abdominal viscera. Supplied by the thoraco-abdominal nerves, subcostal nerve, iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal nerves.

structures.name: Trapezius
structures.summary: Rotates the scapula upwards (descending and ascending parts together) and retracts the scapula (transverse part). Supplied by the accessory nerve (CN XI).

structures.name: Triceps brachii
structures.summary: Extends the elbow. Supplied by the radial nerve.

structures.name: Twelfth rib
structures.summary: The twelfth of the twelve pairs of ribs, a floating rib, with a free front end. Muscles attached include the external oblique, internal oblique and quadratus lumborum.

structures.name: Ulna
structures.summary: The forearm bone on the little-finger side; its upper end forms the point of the elbow. Muscles attached include the flexor digitorum superficialis, flexor digitorum profundus and flexor carpi ulnaris.

structures.name: Ureter
structures.summary: A muscular tube that carries urine from the kidney down to the bladder.

structures.name: Urinary bladder
structures.summary: Stores urine in the pelvis until it is emptied through the urethra.

structures.name: Vastus intermedius
structures.summary: Extends the knee. Supplied by the femoral nerve.

structures.name: Vastus lateralis
structures.summary: Extends the knee. Supplied by the femoral nerve.

structures.name: Vastus medialis
structures.summary: Extends the knee. Supplied by the femoral nerve.

structures.name: Zygomaticus major
actions: Pulls the corners of the mouth up
structures.summary: Draws the angle of the mouth upward and laterally (smiling). Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), zygomatic and buccal branches.

structures.name: Zygomaticus minor
structures.summary: Elevates the upper lip. Supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII), zygomatic and buccal branches.
